speaker_role: former admissions officer (Andrew Hoffman, describes two decades evaluating activity lists for selective colleges, including reference to work at Vanderbilt)
commercial_incentive: Yes - repeatedly promotes the presenter's paid recorded 'Common App boot camp'
key_insights: States admissions officers likely spend only about 60-90 seconds reviewing a student's entire activities list, so front-loading the strongest activities matters

Identifies three dimensions officers look for in the activities section: impact (quantitative or qualitative effect on home/school/community), depth (role/leadership, not necessarily official titles), and longevity (sustained involvement over ~3-4 years, contrasted with a 'junior joiner' who piles on activities only in junior year)
Cautions against overusing quantitative metrics for every activity, since not everything needs a number to be compelling

Explains a significant recent Common App format change: activity descriptions now lead with the organization/group name followed by the role (e.g., 'Computer Science Club, Parker High School, Co-founder'), reversed from the prior year's format that listed the leadership title first - which may catch admissions officers used to the old format off guard

Recommends students with especially distinctive leadership titles consider deliberately reordering fields (e.g., listing a unique title like 'Wisconsin Upper Michigan District Governor' before the org name) to make the most impressive detail most visible, despite this diverging from the form's default field order

Recommends structuring the 10 available activity slots strategically: front-load the 5 most significant/narrative-relevant activities on 'page one,' include at least one or two four-year-sustained commitments, and place shorter-term, less central, or unrelated activities in slots 6-10
Notes the hours-per-week question changed to ask about the busiest time of year (not an annual average), so reported hours may look high without students needing to worry about consistency

Suggests using the 'additional information' section for one or two especially significant activities where the 150-character limit can't fully capture their significance, but advises being succinct and not duplicating a resume there
specific_numbers_or_facts: Admissions officers reportedly spend about 60-90 seconds reviewing a student's activities list (presenter's professional estimate)
The Common App activities section allows up to 10 entries; officers reportedly want to see sustained involvement (~3-4 years) in at least a few of them (presenter)
notable_or_distinctive: The detailed walkthrough of this cycle's specific Common App field-order change (organization name now before role, reversed from prior years) and the tactic of intentionally reordering fields for standout titles is a concrete, mechanically specific tip not found in generic activities-list advice.
reliability_notes: Presenter has a clear commercial incentive (repeated plug for a paid boot camp); claims about officer review time (60-90 seconds) and the described Vanderbilt cheerleading-recruitment anecdote are presented as professional experience without independent sourcing, and Common App form details are current only as of this video's stated cycle and could change in future years.
